body: @SamMousa, transaction object already can be accessed with `$db->transaction`, but there is only one and the same Transaction object. Any way it will be either commited or rollback'ed inside `transaction()` method. So, using `commit()` or `rollback()` in such manner will broke nested transactions.
Commit and rollback support nesting just fine, I don't see how this would break it.

Ah, I figured out the problem!
`Connection::transaction()` checks `isActive()` to see if it should commit / rollback.
Instead it should inspect the actual isolation level.

For this to be implemented we need to make `private $_level` accessible some how.
Some options for this:
- Normal getter (isolationLevel is currently write-only).
- Add parameter to `getIsActive` to check if the transaction is active at  the given `isolationLevel` (so `$_level >= $level`)

I can implement this if one of these proposals is accepted.
Well, it looks like a bug so yes. Try it starting with unit tests that fail.

IMHO, it's not enought. `Connection::transaction()` should to ensure, that `Transaction::begin()` was called by himself and not by another (recursive) `Connection::transaction()` call. For example, `Transaction::begin()` should to return some unique id to pass it into `Transaction::commit()` and `Transaction::rollback()`, or there should be different `Transaction` objects for each `Connection::beginTransaction()` to prevent call to alien `Transaction::commit()` and `Transaction::rollback()`.

I'm sorry, I have no much free time to implement it and check.

Vovan-VE, there is no need for that since `commit` and `rollback` just decrement `$_level`.. The problem is the checks after the closure don't (and currently can't) properly check if the commit / rollback has been called.

body:
@samdark What approach do you prefer? Readable nesting level, or extra parameter to getIsActive that specifies the isolation level to test against (which defaults to 0, to keep current behavior).
- edit: I confused isolation level and nesting level.
Extra parameter to getIsActive means BC break thus could be applied to 2.1 only.
If it is optional it doesn't break BC right? Anyway, shall I implement `getLevel()` then?
It does break BC even if it's optional. It will cause exception in case of method override in nested class.
Because it is protected. Also, it shouldn't do multiple commits it should only do 1, if you begin a new transaction it is your job to finish it...
